subject: Bubblegum coral
topic: These pink, branching trees, deep in a canyon off Virginia, are bubblegum corals.
script:
These pink, branching trees, deep in a canyon off Virginia, are bubblegum corals.
They get their name from their bright color and their knobby, bubblegum-like tips.
And yes, they're animals, not plants.
Bubblegum corals can grow into giant fans, taller than a person.
They grow very slowly, so big colonies can be hundreds of years old.
Their branches give shelter to crabs, sea stars, fish and many other animals.
This wall of bubblegum coral now sits inside a protected area off the US East Coast.
Off the West Coast, a tiny octopus, only ten centimeters wide, was crawling past another one.
Next to the coral, it looked like a toy.
Would you have guessed these trees were animals?
